Procrustes rotation

Source: R/svt.R
procrs.Rd

The orthogonal rotation (a proper rotation: no reflection) that best carries the centred configuration X onto the centred target in least squares, the target's centre added back (Gower and Dijksterhuis 2004).

Usage

procrs(X, target)

Arguments

X

The configuration to rotate.

target

The target configuration, of the same dimensions.

Value

A list of class procrs: rotated, rotation, scale (the sum of the singular values of \(X_c' T_c\)) and mse.

References

Gower, J. C. and Dijksterhuis, G. B. (2004). Procrustes Problems. Oxford University Press.

See also

Other scaling: amscal(), anchv(), anomin(), bamscl(), bbscal(), bmdsf(), bunfld(), cjrirt(), cmdsf(), cutlns(), dblctr(), dwnom(), dynirt(), indscl(), ipsrec(), irtem(), irtlik(), irtpst(), mdsfit(), mlsmu(), nmdsf(), nombt(), nomll(), nompr(), nomutl(), nrmvec(), optcls(), ordirt(), ordocl(), scboot(), smacf(), smunf(), unfstr(), votagr(), wrdfsh()

Examples

set.seed(1)
A <- matrix(rnorm(20), 10)
procrs(A, A %*% matrix(c(0, 1, -1, 0), 2))$rotation
#>      [,1]          [,2]
#> [1,]    0 -1.000000e+00
#> [2,]    1 -1.110223e-16
